properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 9/19/2023 to EQT ARO LLC in McIntyre Township, Lycoming county. 78a56(a) - TEMPORARY STORAGE - Operator failed to contain regulated substances and wastes used at or generated at a well site in a tank, series of tanks or other storage structures approved by the Department.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: EQT ARO LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 9/19/2023
Violation Code: 78a56(a) - TEMPORARY STORAGE - Operator failed to contain regulated substances and wastes used at or generated at a well site in a tank, series of tanks or other storage structures approved by the Department.
Violation ID: 8159692
Permit API: 081-21880
Unconventional: Yes
County: Lycoming
Municipality: McIntyre Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 9/19/2023
Comments: This inspection was conducted in response to a notification from the operator that on 9/18/23 a leak was discovered in a GPU on Pad A which led to the release of an unknown quantity of produced fluid to the pad surface. I met with EQT representative Zac Subra upon arriving on Pad A. He showed me where the produced fluid leak occurred inside of GPU #3. He also showed me where the fluid overflowed the interior containment of the GPU and flowed outside of the GPU and onto the pad surface to the southwest of the GPU. A Waste Management crew was excavating the impacted area of the pad during this inspection. Mr. Subra said that the fluid appears to have traveled a couple of inches into the pad surface and then moved toward the southwest pad edge under the surface. A sump present in the stormwater channel along the southwest side of the pad had fluid in it with an electrical conductivity (EC) of 700 uS/cm. Mr. Subra stated that the initial EC reading taken in this sump was approximately 700 uS/cm and later it increased to approximately 1700 uS/cm. A smaller puddle of fluid approximately 25 feet to the north in the channel had an EC of 760 uS/cm during this inspection. No other fluid was observed in the channel or on the pad surface. The Department recommends vacuuming out the fluid in the southwest stormwater channel.Mr. Subra said that they plan to pursue Act 2 remediation due to the unknown volume of the release. Environmental consultant Penn E and R was present during this inspection. Mr. Subra said that Penn E and R were performing electrical conductivity screening and would take samples for the Act 2 remediation. Violations noted against permit 081-21855 for the produced fluid release to the surface of Pad A.Violations remain outstanding for the produced fluid release to Pad B from 2/21/23.

properties.content:
Report Details
Operator Range Resources Appalachia Llc

Violation Code 78.91(a) - PLUGGING - GENERAL PROVISIONS - Upon abandoning a well, the owner or operator failed to plug the well to stop the vertical flow of fluids or gas within the well bore under 25 Pa. Code ?? 78.92 ? 78.98 or an approved alternate method.
Violation ID 775787
Permit API 033-27140
Unconventional Y
County Clearfield
Municipality Morris Twp
Inspection Type Plugging(Includes Plugged/Mined Through)
Inspection Date 2017-01-04
Comments Inspection of Range’s Hess 1H in Morris Twp. Clearfield County conducted January 4, 2017 at approximately 10 am. I met with Kyle Thomas from Range on the pad for a follow-up inspection in regards to pressure on the 5 ½” csg’s annulus. When I pulled on location he had the annulus shut-in to a digital crystal gauge, reading ~200 PSI after being shut-in for approximately 15 minutes reportedly. Pressure was still increasing at 20 minutes to ~245 PSI and it was decided to bleed off pressure to vent tank to avoid overpressure on the 9 5/8” shoe. I tied a ½” pex fitting with hose connected to an Altair 5x gas meter; 100% methane detected. We discussed possible migration pathway to surface, uncertain at the moment. I advised for Range to take a gas sample of the annulus for analysis to help aid in finding the source of the gas. Two more personnel from Range showed up and took some photos of the well. The operator is likely to commence remedial operations in the spring as requested when the weather is more cooperative for operations rendering a better chance of success. The operator is advised to grab a gas sample come up with an approved procedure in the meantime for addressing the issue of gas on the prod csg annulus. Violations outstanding, 78.91 Plugging.

Comments: Today I conducted a routine inspection at the Varner 2 well. The access road was maintained and in good condition. The well head was maintain with no leaks or defects observed. Production tanks in good condition and were inside containment at the compressor station. No leaks or defects observed at the compressor stations equipment. The site is currently producing.During the inspection I discovered a slide on the Northside of the Varner 2 pad. The slip appeared to be a minor slide where the top soil slid off the slope. The size is approximately 40 feet in length x 15 feet in width. The slide exposed the slopes rock and dirt allowing for erosion. The well pads geo mat/ liner was also exposed at the edges. The slide appeared to be an old slide that settled and became stable. The area had thick vegetation and the landowner established a deer stand on the bench created by the slide. The well was spudded on 02/27/2014. The permit was issued on 08/09/2013 and expired on 08/09/2014. No waterway was impacted by the slide. The pipeline from the well head going to the compressor may be under the slide area. No pipe was exposed in the slide area so could not confirm the exact location of where the pipe was laid. The slide appeared to be just a surface slip with no deep scarp, so no immediate threat was observed at the time of inspection. No equipment or infrastructure are in the path of the slide.

Comments: This well was in production at the time of inspection. There were several pieces of farming equipment staged on the edges of the pad and there was garbage piles located on the far side of the pad. The well head was properly equipped with a well ID tag and the site posting was intact at the entrance to the well road. The AST had several holes located in the sides and top. The well also appeared to be discharging gas into the AST at the time of inspection. Merchbaker reached out to OWS to gather information about this and has yet to hear back.The secondary containment of the AST was holding approximately 2ft of water at the time of inspection. Merchbaker spoke with the landowner and he stated that the farm equipment was his and that he would move it if necessary. After speaking to the landowner this individual left in a hurry according to the landowner. Merchbaker will be following up on this site.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 12/07/2022 to BULL RUN RESOURCES LLC in Hamilton Twp, McKean county. 78.54 - GENERAL REQUIREMENTS - Operator failed to control and dispose of fluids, residual waste and drill cuttings, including tophole water, brines, drilling fluids, drilling muds, stimulation fluids, well servicing fluids, oil, and production fluids in a manner that prevents pollution of the waters of the Commonwealth.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: BULL RUN RESOURCES LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 12/07/2022
Violation Code: 78.54 - GENERAL REQUIREMENTS - Operator failed to control and dispose of fluids, residual waste and drill cuttings, including tophole water, brines, drilling fluids, drilling muds, stimulation fluids, well servicing fluids, oil, and production fluids in a manner that prevents pollution of the waters of the Commonwealth.
Violation ID: 977708
Permit API: 083-47206
Unconventional: No
County: McKean
Municipality: Hamilton Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 12/07/2022
Comments: This inspection was conducted upon being notified by Bull Run Resources that a crude oil release had occurred from a gathering line located at this well site.Upon my arrival on the well site, Eric Clancy of Bull Run explained that a pinhole formed in a steel gathering line located behind the location (east-northeast of the well, GPS coordinate 41.80141N 78.85587W). It appears that crude oil has been discharging from this pinhole at a minimal rate for an unknown period of time.Bull Run has repaired the failure in the gathering line, which has stopped the discharge. Oil soaked soil that was excavated to locate and repair the line remains staged on the well site. Crude oil traveled alongside the southeastern corner of the location for approximately 30 feet before reaching a roadside ditch that runs along the southern edge of the spur road. Evidence of crude oil was observed across an approximate 125 foot stretch of this ditch. Field screening with a PID meter did not detect appreciable VOC readings downslope of 41.80182N 78.85616W. Oil soaked leaves and a thin layer of oil soaked soil have been excavated from the southeastern perimeter of the well site and the ditch, this material is staged on the side of the road.Bull Run has constructed an underflow dam near the southern corner of the well site and has placed numerous absorbent pads on pockets of free crude that remain in the excavated area where the line was unearthed and in the ditch. I suggested to Eric that an additional underflow dam be constructed in the ditch downslope of the point where crude has thus far migrated as a preventive measure. Additional underflow dams and/or absorbent pads/booms should also be considered elsewhere across the impacted area to improve the initial containment efforts. Finally, Eric and I discussed the potential excavation of additional soil in the immediate vicinity of the gathering line, given the presence of visible product in this area. All methods of containment should be regularly monitored and maintained.At the time of this inspection, it is estimated that approximately 10 tons of oil soaked soil and leaf litter have been excavated and are in need of disposal. Additional soil excavation will likely be conducted throughout upcoming remediation activities. At this time, the evidence available suggests that less than one barrel of crude oil was released and no watercourses were impacted by this release.It is requested that Bull Run provide a remediation plan and keep the Department apprised of any developments that pertain to the cleanup of the remaining residual crude oil associated with this release. Upcoming inspections will be conducted to evaluate remediation efforts and determine if additional measures are required.This well is a conventional well, equipped for production with a pump jack. A site ID sign is posted on the jack. The coordinates for this well were updated as part of this inspection.

Unconventional: No

Inspection Date: 1/10/2023
Comments: Routine field inspection performed in late afternoon with cold, cloudy weather conditions, and 32 degrees. Last inspection performed on 8/6/18, more than 4 years ago. Wellhead is located in field ~120' NNE of surface/ground production equipment (photo #1). The wellhead is in close, visible proximity to the production facility (photo #2). At the wellhead the surface casing valve is open, lower right side production tubular valve cracked open to port with closed valve to port and plumbed to domestic house gas meter/drip run, open valve to meter and to drip with open valve to supply after drip, production tubular left side valve is closed, upper production tubular is plumbed with a closed valve union, and the production tubular plumbed on left side (opposite meter) of head to sales/surface equipment with open valve; annulus is exposed and vented to the atmosphere with plumbed tubular sticking out of ground and open valve union (photos #3, #4, and #5). Pressure gauge functioning atop domestic house gas meter reading ~4 psi and Meter reading (photos #6 and #7). No Well label/marker is affixed to wellhead. The wellhead is in close, visible proximity to the production facility and does not require a well label/marker (photo #2). Some trace to moderate corrosion at the wellhead on the production/surface casing steel unions, lubricator, and tubulars. The surface/ground production facility, one 100 bbl steel tank, and one 50 bbl poly tank all contained by a shallow earthen dike (photo #8). Valve open on main tubular feeding facility with cracked open valves to and from separator (photo #9). A functioning pressure gauge present atop separator reading ~90 psi (photo #10). A 31-day production chart is present, with markings dated 12/30/22 (photo #11). Well posting signage affixed to steel tank with all information about well and current Operator present, except the Operator contact address information (photo #12). Fair to moderate corrosion on ground production unit equipment and tank. Notice of violation (NOV) issued for Well posting OGA3211(G). The Department is requesting Operator add contact address information to the permanent well posting signage affixed at the surface production facility. The Operator has not submitted 2021 Mechanical Integrity Assessment (MIA) for this well. No MIA submitted by the Operator for 2021, 2020, and 2019. The last MIA value officially submitted was back in 2018 stating 40 psig. Notice of violation (NOV) issued for Operating Wells - Mechanical Integrity reporting 78.88(e). The Operator submitted annual production reported (APR) in 2021 of 103 Mcf recorded over 365 days. This is an active, producing well.

Unconventional: Yes

Inspection Date: 6/06/2024
Comments: This inspection was conducted in response to a notification from the operator of the discovery of a release of an estimated 20 gallons of a mixture of produced fluid and fresh water. According to the notification, fluid with electrical conductivity (EC) of 10-13 mS/cm was discovered on the pad surface in an area southeast of the well heads when secondary containment was removed from the pad surface. The notification also stated that a shallow trench has been dug along the southeast edge of the secondary containment to collect any additional fluid with elevated EC that may leach out from beneath the containment. The area impacted by the release was estimated to be 30 ft by 50 ft. I met with company man Steven Spitler upon arriving on location. It rained heavily during this inspection. The EC of the fluid present in the trench along the southeast edge of the well head secondary containment was between 4.03 mS/cm and 5.06 mS/cm. The 30 ft by 50 ft area of the pad surface reported to have been impacted by the release southeast of the well heads had puddles of fluid with EC readings between 2.48 mS/cm and 4.00 mS/cm. A vaccum truck was sucking up fluid from the impacted area of the pad surface during this inspection. Other areas of the pad surface had puddles of fluid with EC readings between 856 uS/cm to 1990 uS/cm. According to the company man, excavation of this area was going to be completed by Tobias Machining, present on site during this inspection, and characterization of the site would be conducted by Penn E and R who was en-route to the site during this inspection. The Department requests a justification for the estimated release volume. The Department recommends continuing to vacuum up fluid with elevated EC from the pad surface. Violations noted against permit 081-21945 for the 6/6/24 reported release. Violations remain outstanding against permit 081-21946 for the 5/8/24 release discovered by the Department. These violations will be closed upon attainment of Act 2 remediation standards.

Comments: The Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted an incident inspection of Southwestern's (SWN's) Greenzweig GU-D (Reeve-Sutton) well pad located in Herrick Township, Bradford County on 11/30/2023 at 1030 hours. The weather was 38 degrees with mostly clear skies. The inspection was conducted in response to a release reported to the DEP by SWN. DEP Environmental Trainees, Erica Lutz and Evan Buck, accompanied me during the inspection.SWN reported to the DEP reporting hotline that at ~0300 hours on 11/30/2023 a release of >5 gallons of coolant (ethylene glycol) was spilled to the pad surface at their GU-D (Reeve-Sutton) site. Onsite today, SWN reported that repairs were made to the compressor unit's exhaust manifold after a small leak was noticed, which was all captured by the secondary containment skid. After repairs were complete, the reservoir was refilled with coolant and ended up overtopping the reservoir tank. The overtopping coolant was captured by the secondary containment skid but the skid ended up overtopping as well, causing the release to the pad surface. During this inspection, the majority of the impacted material had been collected but further recovery was underway. SWN reported that glycol test kits would be utilized to confirm that the entire portion of the release was recovered. See photos #1 and 2 for an overview of the release area. No evidence would suggest that any portion of the release was able to escape the gravel surface of the pad.Later in the day, SWN reported via email that the release was further calculated and reported a final release volume of 4-5 gallons of coolant was able to escape secondary containment. The final cleanup photos prior to backfilling are attached (photos #3 and 4) and were provided by the operator.Violations of the following are cited as IMMEDIATELY CORRECTED against API #015-20621:SWMA 301CSL 402(b)25 Pa. Code 78a.56aWe departed the site at 1120 hours.

Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety

Unconventional: Yes

Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 1/29/2024
Comments: On January 29, 2024, inspection conducted at the Fatur Well Pad in Salem Township, Westmoreland County. This inspection was conducted to follow-up to IR 3700597, which was conducted by DEP WQS at OGI request. During this inspection, a pink oily substance with elevated conductivity was discovered on the ground next to the onsite GPU unit and within its secondary containment. Violations were issued as a result. The following was observed:The Act 9 sign was installed at the entrance of the access road and was not obstructed from view by vegetation, in accordance with 78a.55 (see photo 1). The access road and well pad appeared to be stable at the time of inspection, with no concerns relating to accelerated erosion or sedimentation (see photos 2 and 3). The compressor noted in IR 3700597 had rags remaining within its secondary containment, soaking up what appears to be a petroleum based substance (see photos 4 and 6). However, it is on the verge of overflowing (see photo 7). No elevated conductivity readings were gathered from this substance (see photo 8), and there did not appear to be any staining on the ground around it. The well head onsite (well 10H) was equipped with a well tag and appeared to be in production (see photos 13 and 14). Pooling was observed on the ground around the well head, however this appeared to be snowmelt due to the low conductivity and lack of discoloration (see photo 15). A Hugill's dumpster was observed on the eastern side of the pad dripping a dark fluid onto the ground (see photo 16). Although this fluid was not elevated in conductivity, the DEP recommends that this is addressed by the operator and necessary remediations are conducted if this is a regulated substance. The pink oily fluid observed during the time of IR 3700597 remains in the GPU secondary containment. The conductivity of this substance read 15,990 Microsiemens at the time of inspection (see photo 18). The disconnected hose and pink tinted substance remains on the gravel behind the GPU unit. The conductivity of this substance and/or ground surface read 724 Microsiemens at the time of inspection (see photo 19). The gear lubricant container holding a substance of similar coloration remains adjacent to the GPU unit (see photo 20). What appears to be a pump attached to the GPU unit was observed to be completely frosted over at the time of inspection (see photo 21). What appears to be an additional pump in disuse was observed on the ground adjacent to the GPU unit. A background soil conductivity reading was taken at the edge of the woods adjacent to the eastern side of the pad, which read 155.5 Microsiemens. Of the five additional tanks and equipment placed in secondary containment onsite that were not previously noted (see photos 3, 9, 11, 12, and 22), three of them appeared to be holding rainwater at the time of inspection. This does not comply with 25 PA Code 78a64a, as they appear to be reduced in capacity by at least 10 percent at the time of inspection, increasing the likelihood of discharge to the ground in the event of a spill. The ERP and PPC plan were found in the mailbox attached to the Act 9 sign (see photos 24 and 25).The DEP recommended in IR 3700597 that the operator ensure the structural integrity of the all production equipment is sound and properly contain and dispose of any production related fluid in accordance with current regulations to prevent any future pollution events. The DEP also recommended in IR 3700597 that the operator assess the red tinted fluid observed on the ground near the GPU as well as inside of the containment and remediate any spills in accordance with current regulations.Based on observations from this inspection, it appears that not all necessary corrective actions has been taken for site to comply with current regulations. Violations remain outstanding, additional violations may be forthcoming pending receipt and review of operator response.

properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: PENNECO OIL CO INC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 4/08/2024
Violation Code: 91.34(A) - ACTIVITIES UTILIZING POLLUTANTS - Failure to take necessary measures to prevent the substances from directly or indirectly reaching waters of this Commonwealth, through accident, carelessness, maliciousness, hazards of weather or from another cause.
Violation ID: 8182723
Permit API: 129-28783
Unconventional: No
County: Westmoreland
Municipality: Upper Burrell Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 4/08/2024
Comments: On April 8, 2024, inspection conducted on the Tutelo 2 well in Upper Burrell Township, Westmoreland County. This inspection was conducted in response to a spill that reportedly occurred the day prior to this inspection at 7:00 PM, and was reported to the Department that same evening at approximately 9:00 PM by Penneco representative Marc Jacobs (see attached Spill Report). The Department spoke over the phone with Mr. Jacobs while en route to the well site, who explained that a dry-rotted high-pressure hose connected to the well ruptured and released from 1 to 2 barrels of oil onsite. He subsequently explained that Penneco representatives were working nearby when they heard the hose rupture and were able to initiate a prompt response. Present with the Department during this inspection were Woodard and Curran consultants Matt Kapral and Clayton Hefner. Additional representatives from Penneco and Woodard and Curran were also onsite.This inspection report is part 1 of 2, covering the Department's inspection in response to this incident.The following was observed:The access road to the well site appeared to be stable at the time of inspection, with no observed evidence of accelerated erosion or sedimentation (see photo 1). This access road is shared with the Tutelo 1 (129-23915) well site. Materials were staged along the access road for installation of CFS (see photo 2). An unnamed stream or tributary was observed approximately 150 feet south of the well site that flows through a culvert underneath the access road. An oil absorbent boom was observed in this location (see photo 3). The Department spoke with Mr. Kapral and Mr. Hefner who explained that seven additional oil absorbent booms were placed across the unnamed stream or tributary downslope of the cross-culvert under the access road. They further explained that a sheen was observed where the first oil absorbent boom was placed upstream from the access road culvert. Peatmoss was spread on impacted areas not yet excavated onsite (see photos 5 and 6). Brush clearing was conducted on the slope east of the well site to remove impacted vegetation and prepare for excavation of impacted soil (see photos 7 and 8). Minor excavation work had been conducted upon arrival to site to contain impacted material, according to onsite representatives (see photos 9 and 18). Additional excavations were conducted while the Department was onsite. Onsite brine tanks appeared to be sound at the time of inspection (see photo 10). A large tarp was laid west of well site for placement of excavated impacted material (see photo 11). Heavy oil staining was observed on the ground around the well head upon arrival to site (see photo 14). It was equipped with a well tag, and the operator's information was posted on the separator (see photos 16 and 17). The aforementioned sheen was observed upstream of the access road culvert, with fluid beading on the wet rocks in this location (see photos 19 and 20). Due to observations made in this location, the Department subsequently collected water samples in this location. While the Department sampled, CFS installations were conducted (see photos 21 and 22). The overall size of the impacted ground area appeared to be approximately 100 feet by 100 feet at the well site, with approximately 100 additional feet of the access road also being impacted. An oil odor was detectable within an approximate 150 foot radius of the well site. Based on observations from this inspection, remediation in accordance with the requirements of Act 2 is recommended. Violations are being issued in response to observations made during this inspection. Additional violations may be forthcoming pending receipt of analytical results from samples collected during this inspection. Please see IR 3742855 for inspection report documenting the Department's collection of aqueous samples from the onsite unnamed stream or tributary.

Report Details

Violation Code: 78a57(a) - CONTROL, STORAGE AND DISPOSAL OF PRODUCTION FLUIDS - Operator failed to collect brine and other fluids produced during operation of the well in a tank, series of tanks, or other device approved by the Department for subsequent disposal or reuse.
Violation ID: 8213980
Permit API: 051-24701
Unconventional: Yes
County: Fayette
Municipality: German Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 1/13/2025
Comments: On January 13, 2025, the Department conducted an Incident Inspection of EQT's Herriott Well Pad after a spill was reported to the emergency hotline at 1:50pm on January 12, 2025. According to the spill report and a verbal conversation with Logan Dominick of EQT via the phone, at 1pm on 1/12/2025, a truck drove over a hose breaking the coupling on the hose releasing production fluids. Mr. Dominick stated that 90% of the spill occurred on containment and approximately 10% spilled off of containment. Mr. Dominick estimated that 10 gallons spilled and stated that SPSI scraped approximately 6 inches of the well pad in the spill area as well as vacuumed up the containment and placed all contaminated materials into a dumpster on site.At the time of this inspection EQT representative Jeremy Barber was on site and inform the Department that Flowback was currently occurring. At the time of this inspection, the Department observed a section of the pad that was scrapped adjacent to two frack tanks that were in containment. The Department also observed a dumpster adjacent to the spill area. In the middle of the spill area appeared to be a strip of containment that had hoses in it. Mr. Barber pointed out that the open hose was the one that was ran over and caused the spill. The Department did not observe any holes or tears in the hose containment or the frack tank containment and the containments appeared to be dry.Background conductivity readings were taken adjacent to the well pad on the perimeter and some vegetation (0.289mS) and then readings were taken in the spill area that was scraped (0.0945 mS, 0.0386, 0.0416mS), then a reading was taken outside but directly adjacent to the spill area (0.0036 mS). Mr. Barber informed the Department that the area underneath these containments had not been scraped yet and that as soon as Flowback is completed, they will be pulled, the area beneath them will be scraped, and any contaminated material will be properly disposed of. The Department took conductivity readings at the edge/underneath this containment to determine if this area is contaminated, and the readings are as follows: 3.34 mS and 1.649 under/adjacent to the containment of the frack tanks where the spill occurred, and 13.98 mS under/adjacent to the containment where the hose is and where the spill originated. The soil conductivity readings in the spill area where the ground has been scraped, is comparable to the background reading and therefore appears to be remediated in accordance with the Department's policy for small spills, however, the readings in the area at the edge of/underneath the containment lining were elevated compared to the background reading and therefore appears to still be contaminated. The Department verbally recommended to Mr. Barber that the containment be lifted and materials be scraped as soon as possible. Mr. Barber informed The Department that SPSI will be back on site today and they will continue to remediate the release in accordance with policies. Mr. Barber also stated that photo documentation of continued remediate efforts will be supplied to the Department as soon as it is available. The Department is requesting the Operator submit a written response within seven (7) days of the receipt of this report. This written response should include an incident report, a timeline of remedial measures, and plan for remediation of the spill or release. The Department is requesting how the Operator quantified the amount spilled. The Department also requests the waste manifest from the site remediation be submitted upon receipt.Based on today's inspection and the spill not being completely remediated yet, violations are being issued for an approximately 10 gallon release of production fluid from a hose onto the well pad.

Permit API: 085-23523
Unconventional: No
County: Mercer

Inspection Type: Complaint Inspection
Inspection Date: 6/24/2021
Comments: Stopped to inspect this gas well a day after the reported spill incident as the result of a piece of farm equipment had that had hit this gas well causing a release of gas and production fluids. The incident happened at approximately 11 AM on June 23, 2021. I was notified the same day by phone at 1 PM by Matt Kleese from Diamond Energy. The summary of the situation is as follows: the gas well was hit by a piece of equipment being operated by Centerra Co-op for the farmer. The tubing on the gas well was completely sheared off by this piece of equipment. Nobody was injured. The gas well had an approximate pressure of 680 psi and vented for approximately 1 minute after the incident before it just basically stopped. Centerra is taking full responsibility and is handling the clean-up. The gas well was presently shut in with a new piece of tubing in place. The operator reported less than one barrel of oil that was released from this well. It was difficult to say how much oil was released from a spill like this where the production fluids are spread over the land area by the venting (blowing) gas. There was a 60 yard x 35 yard area around the well where the oil mist had been scraped off the ground surface. No residual of any kind was seen. There was however an oil residual on the leaves of the trees for an approximate 80 yard stretch. I contacted Jason Nowakowski from Centerra regarding the clean-up and the ownership of the trees on the field edge. He said they have hauled the soil back to their shop for proper disposal. He also said that he would have to get back to me on the ownership of the trees.
